Now speaking

Morning, George — it's Saturday the twenty-second, and Athens is going to be a scorcher again, so this one's a stay-cool, take-it-slow kind of day.

The big picture's heavier than the mood outside: the standoff between the US and Iran sharpened hard overnight, and Russia hit a shopping mall in Zelensky's hometown.

— personal items —

Let's start abroad, because it's the story of the morning.

The confrontation between Washington and Tehran took a sharp turn: the US rolled out a fresh round of sanctions aimed at Iran and anyone still trading with it, Trump publicly told Tehran to raise, in his words, the white flag of surrender, and Iran answered that it's shifting to a fully offensive military posture.

On top of that, the US Navy is tightening a blockade of Iranian ports, having already turned back dozens of commercial ships.

It's the tensest this has been in weeks, so worth keeping half an eye on.

Then a brutal one out of Ukraine.

Russia launched what's being called a double-tap drone strike on a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih — that's Zelensky's own hometown — killing at least fourteen people and wounding well over a hundred.

The cruelty is in the design: a second wave hit half an hour after the first, timed to catch the rescuers and firefighters who'd rushed in.

Children are among the injured.

And your science hit, a genuinely useful one: a big Swedish study following more than three hundred and seventy thousand people found that people who took part in colorectal cancer screening had a forty-three percent lower risk of dying from the disease.

That's a huge number for something as simple as showing up for the test — a good reminder that screening quietly saves a lot of lives.

Over in AI, it's still quiet right at the very top — no new flagship from the big labs overnight.

The story worth your attention as a builder is on the open side: Google's Gemma family of open models just crossed one billion downloads, with more than a hundred thousand community-made variants built on top.

To mark it they've launched an "Awesome Gemma" directory on GitHub — basically a curated hub of the best fine-tunes, tools, and tutorials people have built.

If you ever want a capable model you can run locally without paying per token, that's the ecosystem to raid.

Athens today: clear, dry, and properly hot — around twenty-six first thing, climbing to a high near thirty-six in the afternoon, then barely easing to the mid-twenties overnight.

No rain to speak of, just a light northerly breeze swinging round to the south later.

That dry heat keeps fire risk high across Attica, so steer clear of dry brush if you head out.

Sunset's just before eight.

— personal items —

And to leave you a touch sharper.

Word of the day: dyno — short for a dynamic move, where you launch off the wall with both feet leaving the rock to snatch a hold you can't reach any other way; all-or-nothing, and deeply satisfying when it sticks.

And a fact to sit with: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the first Moon landing than she did to the building of the Great Pyramid.

The pyramid was already ancient history to her.

That's your Saturday — heavy news abroad, a blazing hot and slow day at home, and nothing on your plate you didn't put there.

Drink water and enjoy the quiet.
